newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Treasury may buy debt early from RBA.
newsitem.headline: Australian Treasury may buy debt early from RBA.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said on Wednesday that any early retirement of debt to gross-up the aggregate new debt issue program would be undertaken from bonds held by the Reserve Bank of Australia which were near maturity.

Speaking to a financial markets conference Tony Hinton, first assistant secretary of the Treasury's investment and debt division, said further down the track reverse bond tenders to purchase longer dated securities from the market were an option.

"For the present, the intention is that any early repurchases would be undertaken from the Reserve Bank's portfolio of CGS (Commonwealth Government Securities) and would be limited to stocks with no more than 12 to 18 months till maturity," he said.
Any such transactions would be priced at prevailing market rates.

"Of course, as any early redemptions would be financed by the issue of new stock, any such transactions would have no effect on the Commonwealth's net call on the market, nor on the stock of Commonwealth debt outstanding," Hinton said.

The possible early retirement of debt would help better manage the Government's funding risk and would help maintain liquidity across the curve, in the face of smaller debt issuance programs as a result of ongoing fiscal consolidation.
The strategy was announced in the 1997/98 budget, delivered in May, and had also been contained in the previous budget, Hinton said.

"Looking further forward, it is possible that the option of conducting reverse tenders direct in the market for stocks further out on the curve might need to be considered, although the need for, and timing of, any such move is quite uncertain at
In a reverse bond tender, the Treasury offers to buy specified securities, and holders submit the price at which they would be willing to sell them.
A reverse bond tender was conducted in the 1989/90 fiscal year, when the Commonwealth Budget was last in surplus, at which Treasury repurchased A$160 million of selected stocks.
As the primary objective of such a move would be to build and enhance liquidity of benchmark stocks, reverse tender stocks would need to be selected carefully, Hinton said.
"Stocks from those years where there are currently two benchmark lines on issue would be an obvious point to start such an exercise," Hinton said.
